+    'If the ticket turns out larger than written, stop with a report of what you found instead of widening the change.',
+  ].join('\n')
+}
+
+/** The line the reviewer's answer opens with, and the pattern that reads it back. */
+const REVIEW_VERDICT_LINE = /^[ \t]*verdict:[ \t]*(approve|reject)[ \t]*$/im
+
+/** The first sentence of the reviewer's standing instruction, by which a scripted route recognizes a review. */
+export const REVIEW_MARKER = 'You are the independent reviewer of one change to a repository.'
+
+/**
+ * The reviewer's standing instruction. It states the answer format the verdict
+ * is read back from, so a change here without a matching change to the verdict
+ * pattern rejects every change.
+ */
+export const REVIEW_INSTRUCTION = [
+  `${REVIEW_MARKER} You did not make it and cannot reach the session that did: the next two messages are the whole record you have.`,
+  '',
+  'The first is the ticket the implementer worked from. The second is the evidence: the diff the implementer committed, the messages of its commits, and the output of every check the change was measured by.',
+  '',
+  'Answer with this line first, then your reasons on the lines after it:',
+  '',
+  'verdict: approve',
+  '',
+  'Use `approve` when the diff does what the ticket asks, stays inside the ticket\'s scope, and the checks passed. Use `reject` when it does not do what the ticket asks, changes more than the ticket asks, or the evidence cannot show that it does. The ticket describes the tree as intake saw it; the diff, the commit messages, and the check outputs are the current facts, so judge the diff against the ticket\'s problem and required behaviour rather than against a step the tree already satisfied. Decide on what you were given; there is nothing further to ask for.',
+].join('\n')
+
+/**
+ * The ticket as the reviewer reads it.
+ * @param ticket - the ticket.
+ * @returns the second message of the review.
+ */
+export function reviewTicketText(ticket: Ticket): string {
+  return [
+    `<ticket id="${ticket.id}" kind="${ticket.kind}" seat="${ticket.seat}">`,
+    `title: ${ticket.title}`,
+    `task: ${ticket.task}`,
+    `scope: ${ticket.scope.join(', ')}`,
+    'acceptance:',
+    ...ticket.acceptance.map(check => `- ${check.id}: ${check.run}`),
+    '</ticket>',
+  ].join('\n')
+}
+
+/** One check's outcome as the reviewer reads it. */
+export interface ReviewedCheck {
+  readonly id: string
+  readonly status: string
+  readonly evidence: string
+}
+
+/**
+ * The evidence as the reviewer reads it: the bounded diff, the bounded
+ * messages of the branch's commits, then every check with its status and
+ * bounded output. The commit messages are the implementer's own account of
+ * the change, committed with it; nothing of the implementer's session is here.
+ * @param diff - `git diff <base> HEAD` of the department branch.
+ * @param commits - `git log <base>..HEAD` of the department branch, messages only.
+ * @param checks - the department's certifying run.
+ * @param maxChars - bound of the diff, of the commit messages, and of each check's evidence.
+ * @returns the third message of the review.
+ */
+export function reviewEvidenceText(diff: string, commits: string, checks: readonly ReviewedCheck[], maxChars: number): string {
+  return [
+    '<diff>',
+    boundHead(diff, maxChars),
+    '</diff>',
+    '<commits>',
+    boundHead(commits, maxChars),
+    '</commits>',
+    '<checks>',
+    ...checks.map(check => `- ${check.id}: ${check.status}\n${boundHead(check.evidence, maxChars)}`),
+    '</checks>',
+  ].join('\n')
+}
+
+/** Keep the head of longer text inside the bound, marking what was dropped. */
+function boundHead(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
+  return text.length <= maxChars ? text : `${text.slice(0, maxChars - 1)}…`
+}
+
+/**
+ * Read the reviewer's verdict out of its answer: the first `verdict:` line
+ * naming `approve` or `reject`, with everything after it as the rationale. An
+ * answer naming neither is a rejection carrying the answer itself, because a
+ * reviewer that did not decide approved nothing.
+ * @param answer - the reviewer's assembled reply text.
+ * @param maxChars - bound of the recorded rationale.
+ * @returns the verdict and its bounded rationale.
+ */
+export function readReviewVerdict(answer: string, maxChars: number): { verdict: 'approve' | 'reject'; rationale: string } {
+  const match = REVIEW_VERDICT_LINE.exec(answer)
+  if (match === null) {
+    const text = answer.trim()
+    return { verdict: 'reject', rationale: boundHead(text === '' ? 'the reviewer answered nothing' : `no verdict line: ${text}`, maxChars) }
+  }
+  const rationale = answer.slice(match.index + match[0].length).trim()
+  return { verdict: match[1] as 'approve' | 'reject', rationale: boundHead(rationale === '' ? 'the reviewer gave no reason' : rationale, maxChars) }
+}
+
+/** The two trailer lines every shipped commit ends with: the model that wrote the change, and the operator's session. */
+export interface CommitTrailers {
+  readonly coAuthor: string
+  readonly session: string
+}
+
+/**
+ * The message one shipped ticket commit carries. The commit is authored and
+ * committed as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`, the repository's rule, so the
+ * enterprise is named in the body.
+ * @param ticket - the ticket.
+ * @param shift - the shift that shipped it.
+ * @param programId - the program whose department delivered it.
+ * @param departmentSessionId - that department's session.
+ * @param reviewSessionId - the review that approved it.
+ * @param trailers - the two trailer lines.
+ * @returns the full message, ending with the trailers.
+ */
+export function shippedCommitMessage(
+  ticket: Ticket,
+  shift: string,
+  programId: string,
+  departmentSessionId: string,
+  reviewSessionId: string,
+  trailers: CommitTrailers,
+): string {
+  return [
+    `${ticket.id}: ${ticket.title}`,
+    '',
+    `Shift: Daliesk shift ${shift}`,
+    `Seat: ${ticket.seat} (${ticket.division})`,
+    `Program: ${programId}`,
+    `Department session: ${departmentSessionId}`,
+    `Review session: ${reviewSessionId}`,
+    `Source: ${ticket.source.path} — ${ticket.source.anchor}`,
+    '',
+    `Co-Authored-By: ${trailers.coAuthor}`,
+    `Claude-Session: ${trailers.session}`,
+  ].join('\n')
+}
+
+/**
+ * The message the shift's own commit carries: its ledger lines and its record.
+ * @param shift - the shift id.
+ * @param shipped - the tickets the commit follows.
+ * @param trailers - the two trailer lines.
+ * @returns the full message.
+ */
+export function shiftCommitMessage(shift: string, shipped: readonly string[], trailers: CommitTrailers): string {
+  const summary = shipped.length === 0 ? 'nothing shipped' : `shipped ${shipped.join(', ')}`
+  return [
+    `chore(enterprise): shift ${shift}, ${summary}`,
+    '',
+    `Daliesk shift ${shift}: its ledger lines and its record under ${SHIFTS_DIR}/.`,
+    '',
+    `Co-Authored-By: ${trailers.coAuthor}`,
+    `Claude-Session: ${trailers.session}`,
+  ].join('\n')
+}
+
+/** Strings shaped like credentials, cut from every recorded byte. */
+const CREDENTIAL_SHAPES = new RegExp([
+  String.raw`\b(?:sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}`,
+  String.raw`|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,})\b`,
+  String.raw`|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----`,
+].join(''), 'g')
+
+/**
+ * Cut credential-shaped strings out of text bound for a committed record.
+ * @param text - the text to record.
+ * @returns the text with each match replaced, and how many were cut.
+ */
+export function redactCredentials(text: string): { text: string; redacted: number } {
+  let redacted = 0
+  const cut = text.replace(CREDENTIAL_SHAPES, () => {
+    redacted += 1
+    return '[redacted]'
+  })
+  return { text: cut, redacted }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The record directory name of one shift: the UTC date it started, then its id.
+ * @param startedAt - the shift's start.
+ * @param shift - the shift id.
+ * @returns `<UTC date>-<shift id>`.
+ */
+export function shiftRecordName(startedAt: Date, shift: string): string {
+  return `${startedAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}-${shift}`
+}
+
+/**
+ * A shift id from its start instant: the UTC clock time and a random suffix,
+ * so two shifts started in one second still record apart.
+ * @param startedAt - the shift's start.
+ * @param suffix - four lower-case hex characters.
+ * @returns `hhmmss-<suffix>`.
+ */
+export function shiftIdFor(startedAt: Date, suffix: string): string {
+  return `${startedAt.toISOString().slice(11, 19).replaceAll(':', '')}-${suffix}`
+}

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

## Decision

[`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/`](../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/README.md) is that engine and `pnpm run enterprise -- shift [--next <n> | --tickets <id,...>] [--implementer route|subagent] [--model <id>] [--push]` ([`scripts/enterprise.ts`](../../../../scripts/enterprise.ts)) launches one shift of it. A shift clones the development branch tip into a scratch directory, borrowing objects from the local repository when it is not shallow; reads and validates the clone's queue and reads its ledger, so selection follows the branch and 

**One program, the ticket as the department.** Each ticket is one goal keyed `t-nnnn`, on the `implementing` preset, under the ticket's own budget, with a standard of the ticket's acceptance commands followed by the engine's checks: `engine-committed` (the branch carries a commit past the base), `engine-scope` (`git diff --name-only <base> HEAD -- . ':(exclude)<prefix>'…` lists nothing, git's own pathspecs deciding what is inside the scope), `engine-whitespace` (`git diff --check`) and `engine-documentation`, the queue policy's `documentationRun` (`pnpm run verify-translation-pairing` for th

**An independent reviewer built the judge's way, not the judge itself.** After a department certifies, a session that never saw it decides: a fresh id with no parent and no seed, the `reviewing` preset — the shipped `judge` preset's arrangement, one persona row, `role: judge` so the read barrier denies it every directory and authority it owns — every global tool restricted away with `tools.restrict({ allow: [] })`, an empty working directory of its own, and a derived history of three messages: the standing instruction, the ticket, and the evidence (the bounded `git diff <base> <revision>`,

**Only approved work reaches the branch, as one commit per ticket.** The approved departments are squashed onto the base in ticket order with `git merge --squash`; a squash that conflicts is reset away and recorded as `conflict` while the rest still assemble. The engine's own commits pass `--no-verify`: the offline install of the worktrees installs the repository's git hooks into the clone, which is right for the departments, whose commits are a contributor's, and wrong for the engine, whose squash was certified by the ticket's acceptance and whose ledger commit is machine-written data — the

**The ledger is the status, the record is the evidence.** `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` gains one line per ticket per shift with the field set shared with the enterprise functions that read it (`type, at, shift, ticket, seat, division, programId, implementer, model, department, checks, review, integration, shipped, reason, tokens, seconds`); a ticket closes on a shipped or rejected line and stays open on any other. The engine's reader takes a line without `type` as a ticket line and skips every other type, because the enterprise functions write their `function` lines into the same file. `data

**A route limit halts the shift on the seam's code.** The driver listens for the first `turn/end` whose failure carries `QUOTA`, the code the seam gives the route's usage-limit notice with the reset as `providerRetryAfterMs` ([the limit wall](2026-09-27-route-limit-halts-the-run.md)), blocks that department's goal with `route-limit` in a microtask — the block is one more append to the session that is publishing the event — so the program ends the attempt without a validation run, lets every later department block on its first refused turn, reviews and assembles nothing, writes `halted: lim

**Safe to rerun unattended.** The wrapper holds `<scratch>/shift.lock` naming its pid; a second shift refuses to start while that pid is alive (exit 4) and replaces the lock of a shift that died; clones a day old are swept when the next shift starts; a shift whose worktrees cannot be prepared or whose program throws still writes every ticket's line and pushes it. The ticket validator takes its queue policy as a parameter (`HARNESS_QUEUE_POLICY` mandates this repository's typecheck and coverage runs, `OPEN_QUEUE_POLICY` nothing beyond the ticket's own checks), so the seeded e2e repository valid

====

[`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/`](../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/README.md) 就是这台引擎，`pnpm run enterprise -- shift [--next <n> | --tickets <id,...>] [--implementer route|subagent] [--model <id>] [--push]`（[`scripts/enterprise.ts`](../../../../scripts/enterprise.ts)）发起它的一个班次。一个班次把开发分支

**一个程序，工单即部门。** 每张工单是一个键为 `t-nnnn` 的目标，使用 `implementing` 预设，处于工单自己的预算之下，其标准是工单的验收命令，其后跟引擎自己的检查：`engine-committed`（分支在基准之后有提交）、`engine-scope`（`git diff --name-only <base> HEAD -- . ':(exclude)<prefix>'…` 列不出任何路径，由 git 自己�

**一位按评审官方式构建的独立评审员，而不是评审官本身。** 部门认证之后，由一个从未见过它的会话作出裁定：全新的 id、没有父会话也没有种子、`reviewing` 预设——即随产品发布的 `judge` 预设的那套安排，一行 persona、`role: judge` 使读屏障拒绝它访问它所拥有的每个目录与每项权限——用 `tools.restr

**只有获批的工作到达分支，每张工单一次提交。** 获批的部门按工单顺序以 `git merge --squash` 压到基准上；squash 冲突的会被重置并记为 `conflict`，其余仍然装配。引擎自己的提交带 `--no-verify`：工作树的离线安装会把仓库的 git 钩子装进克隆，这对部门是对的——它们的提交是贡献者的提交——对引擎却

**台账即状态，记录即证据。** `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` 每班次每工单新增一行，字段集与读取它的企业职能共用（`type, at, shift, ticket, seat, division, programId, implementer, model, department, checks, review, integration, shipped, reason, tokens, seconds`）；工单在已发运或已驳回的行上关闭，在其他任何行上保持开放。引擎的读�

**路由上限依据接缝的码停机。** 驱动监听第一个失败携带 `QUOTA` 的 `turn/end`——接缝赋予路由用量上限通知的码，重置时间作为 `providerRetryAfterMs`（[上限之墙](2026-09-27-route-limit-halts-the-run.md)）——在一个微任务里以 `route-limit` 阻塞该部门的目标——阻塞是对正在发布该事件的会话的又一次追加——于是

**可安全地无人值守重跑。** 包装器持有写明其 pid 的 `<scratch>/shift.lock`；该 pid 存活期间第二个班次拒绝启动（退出码 4），已死亡班次留下的锁会被替换；满一天的克隆在下一个班次启动时清扫；工作树无法准备或程序抛出异常的班次仍然写出每张工单的行并推送。工单校验器把队列策略作为参数（`HA

import re
en='.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md'
zh='.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.zh.md'
s=open(en).read()
a="a ticket closes on a shipped or rejected line and stays open on any other."
assert s.count(a)==1, s.count(a)
s=s.replace(a, a+" `--next <n>` takes the open tickets in queue order: fewest attempts first, a line whose reason starts `halted: limit` not counting as one; then priority; then each division in turn among tickets of the same attempts and priority; then id. A ticket that failed therefore waits until every untried ticket had its turn, and one division's backlog does not hold back another division's tickets of the same priority.")
open(en,'w').write(s)
t=open(zh).read()
b="工单在已发运或已驳回的行上关闭，在其他任何行上保持开放。"
assert t.count(b)==1, t.count(b)
t=t.replace(b, b+"`--next <n>` 按队列顺序取开放工单：尝试次数最少者优先，原因以 `halted: limit` 开头的行不算一次尝试；其次按优先级；再在尝试次数与优先级相同的工单之间让各部门轮流；最后按 id。因此失败过的工单要等每张未尝试的工单都轮到之后才会再被选中，一个部门的积压也不会挡住另一个部门同优先级的工单。")
open(zh,'w').write(t)

fen='examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/README.md'
fzh='examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/README.zh.md'
s=open(fen).read()
a="`--next <n>` takes the first `n` open tickets by priority then id, `--tickets <id,...>` the named ones."
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,"`--next <n>` takes the first `n` open tickets in queue order (fewest attempts, a halt on the usage limit not counting as one; then priority; then each division in turn; then id), `--tickets <id,...>` the named ones.")
open(fen,'w').write(s)
t=open(fzh).read()
b="`--next <n>` 按优先级再按 id 取前 `n` 张未关闭工单，`--tickets <id,...>` 取指定的几张。"
assert t.count(b)==1
t=t.replace(b,"`--next <n>` 按队列顺序取前 `n` 张未关闭工单（尝试次数最少者优先，因用量上限而停机不算一次尝试；其次按优先级；再让各部门轮流；最后按 id），`--tickets <id,...>` 取指定的几张。")
open(fzh,'w').write(t)

den='data/enterprise/README.md'
dzh='data/enterprise/README.zh.md'
s=open(den).read()
a="the `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS` (default 2) highest-priority open tickets"
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,"the next `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS` (default 2) open tickets in the engine's queue order")
open(den,'w').write(s)
t=open(dzh).read()
i=t.find('对优先级最高的 `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS`（默认 2）张开放工单')
assert i>=0
t=t.replace('对优先级最高的 `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS`（默认 2）张开放工单','对按引擎队列顺序排在最前的 `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS`（默认 2）张开放工单')
open(dzh,'w').write(t)
EOF

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

input.description: Cycle records, 24h report, deck panel
input.prompt:
You are working in the DeepSeek Harness repository, which houses "Daliesk", an AI enterprise: a roster of 147 seats in 10 divisions (data/enterprise/roster.json), a ticket queue (data/enterprise/tickets/), a shift engine that ships tickets through reviewed programs (`pnpm run enterprise -- shift`), the ticketless divisions' functions (`pnpm run enterprise:functions`), a self-refilling intake (`pnpm run enterprise:intake`), all recorded in data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl, and a public command deck (apps/command-deck, GitHub Pages https://lbjlincoln.github.io/deepseek-harness/, data from `pnpm run enterprise:publish`). Since 2026-09-28T20:11Z, scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh runs every two hours unattended (a Routine launches it in a dedicated worktree): intake → shift → functions → roster → publish → push, logging only to a container-local file that the repository never sees. At 2026-09-29T15:00Z the operator must be given an honest, reproducible account of what the enterprise did in its first 24 hours unattended. You build that evidence: (1) a durable record of every cycle, (2) a deterministic report over any time window, (3) the deck's "last 24 hours" view.

Read first: CLAUDE.md, docs/testing.md, data/enterprise/README.md, scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh, scripts/enterprise-ledger.ts, scripts/enterprise-publish.ts and its spec, scripts/enterprise-functions.ts (how it reads the GitHub REST API unauthenticated under NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 and maps Branch CI jobs), scripts/enterprise-roster.ts, apps/command-deck/README.md and apps/command-deck/components/enterprise/LedgerPanel.tsx, .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-functions-and-occupancy.md.

## Build

1. Cycle record. The cycle writes data/enterprise/cycles/<cycle id>.json before its final commit and includes it in that commit: cycle id, startedAt, endedAt, the commit the cycle started from and the tip it ended on (before its own final commit), every step in order (name, exit code, UTC time), the shift id(s) the cycle's shift wrote (from ledger lines added during the cycle), counts of the ticket lines by status and the function lines by outcome written during the cycle, and firstFailure. The final push's own outcome cannot be in its own record: the next cycle's record states whether the previous cycle's record reached the remote branch, or say in the README where that is visible. Keep the shell thin: it appends step lines to a temporary file and a TypeScript script (for example scripts/enterprise-cycle-record.ts) builds and validates the JSON. Keep the script's one-function body (`main() {…}; main "$@"`): the cycle pulls the branch, which may rewrite the script while it runs. A record that cannot be written must never stop the cycle; it is recorded as a failed step.
2. Report. `pnpm run enterprise:report -- [--since <ISO>] [--until <ISO>] [--write]` (scripts/enterprise-report.ts), deterministic given the repository state and the CI answers. Over the window it reports: cycles (count, clean, failed by step); ticket lines by status and by division, and the distinct tickets shipped with their commits; each shipped commit's Branch CI verdict, read from the GitHub REST API unauthenticated through the proxy as enterprise:functions does (the runs for that exact head SHA, or else the first later run whose head contains it, stating which; "no run" is a valid answer); seats occupied and active by division, from the roster generator at the window's end; function runs by division and outcome; tokens and seconds. It prints markdown. `--write` writes data/enterprise/reports/<until as YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMZ>.{json,md}. It never claims what the data does not show, and it lists every unknown as unknown.
3. Deck. `enterprise:publish` adds the last-24-hours summary (the report's JSON over [generatedAt − 24h, generatedAt]) to the deck's fixture data, and the deck's Enterprise view shows it: cycles run and their outcomes, tickets shipped by division with commit and CI verdict, and seats active by division. Keep every existing view working (`next build` clean, the deck's own tests). Confirm from the Pages workflow's path filters that the cycle's data push republishes the deck.
4. Tests and docs:
   - Unit tests, with the GitHub API mocked, for the record builder and the report.
   - Docs in both languages: sections for the cycle record and the report in the data/enterprise/README pair, and the deck README pair where it describes views. Re-record each pair with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
   - A bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (Problem, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Verification), or an extension of the functions-and-occupancy note if that is the one home for the fact.
5. Run the report once for real over [2026-09-28T17:03:33Z, now] and put its output in your final report. Do not commit a report file; the operator generates the final one.

## Constraints (the cycles run while you work)

- Work only in your worktree. Do not touch /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/enterprise-cycle, /home/user/enterprise-cycles/, /tmp/dsh-enterprise, or the main tree /home/user/deepseek-harness.
- Do not edit machine-written data: data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl, tickets, shifts, functions and intake records, roster.json.
- The operator is changing the engine: do not edit examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/* or scripts/enterprise.ts.
- Run heavy commands as `flock /tmp/dsh-heavy.lock <cmd>` (typecheck, doc-sync, next build, broad vitest runs, pnpm build). The machine has 4 cores and 15 GB of RAM, shared with the running cycles.
- Never kill a process you did not start, and never kill by pattern.
- Use no web tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, Firecrawl): they block the whole session waiting for approval. GitHub REST reads go through Node's fetch under NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 with the proxy's CA, as enterprise:functions does. Never disable TLS verification.
- Start with `git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt && git reset --hard origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`.
- Commit with `git -c user.name=Claude -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com commit -F <file>`. Every message ends with exactly these two lines, after a blank line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C
- Never push, never open a pull request, and never touch another branch. Never write which model you are into a committed file. Never commit credentials.
- One subscription serves every agent, and its weekly window is near the limit, so be economical:
  - Read excerpts of large files, not whole files.
  - Wait on a long process with ONE background command.
  - Never poll with repeated turns.
  - Foreground `sleep` is blocked.
- Before your final commit, run these gates: `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run knip`, the deck's build and tests, `pnpm run doc-sync`, and your unit tests.
- Finish by 2026-09-29T02:00Z. If time runs short, land the cycle record and the report first, and the deck panel after.

Report at the end: the commit hashes in order, each command you ran and its result, the real report's output, and what you could not verify.

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

7:## Problem
11:## Decision
13:`.github/workflows/branch-ci.yml` runs the same three gate groups the enterprise lanes run (`check:ci:static`, `check:ci:coverage`, `check:ci:consumers`) on hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners on every push of the development branch and on manual dispatch. feat(enterprise): a shift takes tickets in a fair queue order

`--next <n>` took the open tickets by priority then id, so a ticket that
failed was retried at the head of every later shift and could hold a slot
forever, and Harness Core's nine priority-1 tickets ran before any other
division's priority-1 ticket. queueOrder now sorts the open tickets by
attempts (fewest first; a line whose reason starts `halted: limit`, the
engine's LIMIT_HALT_REASON, is not an attempt), then priority, then each
division in turn among tickets of the same attempts and priority, then id.
The driver writes both limit-halt reasons from the same constant. The spec
pins the retry order, the limit exemption and the division turns; the
fixture README pair, the data/enterprise README pair and the engine's Agent
Note pair state the order.

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

pnpm run enterprise:functions   # the functions of the ticketless divisions, appended to the ledger
pnpm run roster                 # the roster over every record and every ledger line
pnpm run enterprise:publish     # the deck's fixtures from the roster and the ledger
```

Each command is idempotent and safe on any later commit: the functions runner appends and never rewrites, records a CI verdict once, and leaves the judges vacant rather than failing when the API cannot be read; the generator reproduces `roster.json` byte for byte over unchanged inputs and restamps it only when a record, a source or a ledger line changed, a moved source failing it with its name before anything is written; the publisher rewrites a fixture only when its bytes change. The engine runs the three in this order after every shift.

## The cycle

[`scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh`](../../scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh) runs the enterprise once, in order: the coordinators' [intake](#intake) when fewer than `ENTERPRISE_MIN_OPEN` tickets (default 8) are open, committed and pushed first so the shift's clone sees the new tickets; one [shift](#shifts) over the next `ENTERPRISE_TICKETS` (default 2) open tickets in the engine's queue order with `--push`; the ticketless [functions](#functions) on the new tip, each heavy gate taking `ENTERPRISE_HEAVY_LOCK` (default `/tmp/dsh-heavy.lock`) only while it runs; `pnpm run roster` and `pnpm run enterprise:publish`; and one commit of the functions' lines and evidence, the roster and the deck data, pushed. Every step runs whatever an earlier step's outcome was, except that an intake the usage limit stopped (exit 3) skips the shift. The cycle exits 4 when another cycle holds its lock, 5 when the checkout has uncommitted changes to tracked files, and otherwise with the first failing step's code; its own commits carry `ENTERPRISE_COMMIT_TRAILERS` when set. The enterprise runs it every two hours from a dedicated checkout of the development branch, so no operator's working tree is written to.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh on a fixed UTC schedule from the checkout it
# is started in, so the enterprise's cycles keep their times when no operator
# session is free to launch them:
#   ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_HOURS   the cycle runs in every UTC hour divisible by
#                               it (default 2);
#   ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_MINUTE  at this minute past such an hour (default 13);
#   ENTERPRISE_CYCLE_LOGS       each cycle's output goes to
#                               <dir>/cycle-<UTC stamp>.log (default
#                               /home/user/enterprise-cycles).
# The environment is passed on to every cycle, ENTERPRISE_COMMIT_TRAILERS
# included. A second scheduler exits 4 while one holds the lock. A cycle that
# is still running at the next slot makes that slot's cycle exit 4 in its own
# log; the scheduler waits for every cycle it starts, so that only happens
# when a cycle was started by hand.
set -u

# The whole body is one function, parsed before it runs: the cycles pull the
# branch, which may rewrite this very file under the running shell.
main() {
  repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
  cd "$repo" || exit 1
  every=${ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_HOURS:-2}
  minute=${ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_MINUTE:-13}
  logs=${ENTERPRISE_CYCLE_LOGS:-/home/user/enterprise-cycles}
  case "$every" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "enterprise-scheduler: ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_HOURS must be a whole number of hours"; exit 2;; esac
  case "$minute" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "enterprise-scheduler: ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_MINUTE must be a whole number of minutes"; exit 2;; esac
  if [ "$every" -lt 1 ] || [ "$every" -gt 24 ] || [ "$minute" -gt 59 ]; then
    echo "enterprise-scheduler: the schedule needs 1 <= hours <= 24 and minute <= 59"
    exit 2
  fi

  exec 8>"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/enterprise-scheduler.lock"
  if ! flock -n 8; then
    echo "enterprise-scheduler: another scheduler holds the lock"
    exit 4
  fi
  mkdir -p "$logs" || exit 1

  while true; do
    local now slot hour
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    slot=$(( now / 3600 * 3600 + minute * 60 ))
    while true; do
      hour=$(( slot / 3600 % 24 ))
      if [ "$slot" -gt "$now" ] && [ $(( hour % every )) -eq 0 ]; then break; fi
      slot=$(( slot + 3600 ))
    done
    echo "enterprise-scheduler: next cycle at $(date -u -d "@${slot}" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    sleep $(( slot - now ))
    local stamp
    stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
    bash scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh > "${logs}/cycle-${stamp}.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null
    echo "enterprise-scheduler: cycle-${stamp} exit=$? at $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
  done
}

main "$@"
exit $?

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

(1) EnvironmentRunRequest.ladder?: readonly { model?: EnvironmentRunModel }[] — attempt i runs on ladder[i-1].model ?? the stamped model; ladder length overrides maxAttempts when present; the runner owns the ModelSelectionRef and sets selection.current before each route attempt (installModelSelection already applies it on the next step), and passes the attempt's model to a delegated child; every EnvironmentRunAttempt records `model`; the stamp gains `ladder` (the list) so the arm identity carries it. (2) Transcript interface: the route implementer keeps its transcript (later attempts continue the session); a subagent implementer drops it (fresh child per attempt) and the follow-up text of a delegated attempt must restate the task prompt before the <validation_failed> directive (today the child receives the directive alone, which is why the product loop recovered 0 of 5 at tier 5). Document that the in-process spawn provider is the route's 'drop' arm and that 'keep' on an out-of-process child needs provider resume (gap). (3) Fleet plan and experiment arm carry `ladder`, digested; scorekeeper rows and observatory columns carry a ladder digest beside model. (4) Keyless e2e in the environment-run fixture (a two-step ladder switching between two cli-mock models, asserting attempts[].model and the restated task in the delegated prompt), snapshot if model-visible text changes, README + docs/subsystems/improvement.md, bilingual Agent Note. Then E5 arms on tier 5 seed 2: start strong (opus×3), cheap-then-strong keep (haiku, opus, opus on route), cheap-then-strong drop (same ladder via spawn), downshift (opus, haiku, haiku).

content.activeForm: Rebuilding the Claude Code route around native tool use
content.description: Root cause of the bench smoke failures: models emit native tool_use for prompt-listed tools, the product answers "No such tool", the two-turn bound ends the query (11/12 queries failed; probes 0/3 sonnet). content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

The budget policy folds only on agent/pre-step, which a delegated cell never reaches. Slice: the runner derives the attempt deadline from the same caps (a wall cap per attempt and per cell forwarded as the delegation's signal timeout; the child's reported usage counted against maxTotalTokens after each attempt), records a budget/breach the same way, and the experiments service refuses a paired plan whose arms would run under different caps. Until it lands, every harness-versus-product comparison on tier 5 must state the asymmetry.

content.description: Spec for the delegated agent (start after #76 merges; both touch packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts). (1) EnvironmentRunRequest.ladder?: readonly { model?: EnvironmentRunModel }[] — attempt i runs on ladder[i-1].model ?? the stamped model; ladder length overrides maxAttempts when present; the runner owns the ModelSelectionRef and sets selection.current before each route attempt (installModelSelection already applies it on the next step), and passes the attempt's model to a delegated child; every EnvironmentRunAttempt records `model`; the stamp gains `ladder` (the list) so the arm identity carries it. (2) Transcript interface: the route implementer keeps its transcript (later attempts continue the session); a subagent implementer drops it (fresh child per attempt) and the follow-up text of a delegated attempt must restate the task prompt before the <validation_failed> directive (today the child receives the directive alone, which is why the product loop recovered 0 of 5 at tier 5). Document that the in-process spawn provider is the route's 'drop' arm and that 'keep' on an out-of-process child needs provider resume (gap). (3) Fleet plan and experiment arm carry `ladder`, digested; scorekeeper rows and observatory columns carry a ladder digest beside model. (4) Keyless e2e in the environment-run fixture (a two-step ladder switching between two cli-mock models, asserting attempts[].model and the restated task in the delegated prompt), snapshot if model-visible text changes, README + docs/subsystems/improvement.md, bilingual Agent Note. Then E5 arms on tier 5 seed 2: start strong (opus×3), cheap-then-strong keep (haiku, opus, opus on route), cheap-then-strong drop (same ladder via spawn), downshift (opus, haiku, haiku).

input.description: Owner requests become enterprise tickets
input.prompt:
You are working in the DeepSeek Harness repository, which houses "Daliesk", an AI enterprise that runs itself. It has a roster of 147 seats in 10 divisions (data/enterprise/roster.json) and a ticket queue (data/enterprise/tickets/T-nnnn.json, validated by scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts). A shift engine (`pnpm run enterprise -- shift`) has each ticket implemented by its seat's department, independently reviewed, and shipped to the development branch. A self-refilling intake (`pnpm run enterprise:intake`, scripts/enterprise-intake.ts plus scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts and the fixture examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-intake/) has the Program Departments coordinators propose tickets when fewer than `--min-open` are open, and admits them deterministically: the validator, an acceptance that fails before the change, dedupe, contiguous ids. scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh runs intake → shift → functions → roster → deck every two hours with no operator. The enterprise's owner cannot yet give it work except by talking to an operator session. You build the owner's channel: a request committed to the repository becomes a ticket at the next cycle, and its status can be read back.

Read first: CLAUDE.md, docs/testing.md, data/enterprise/README.md, scripts/enterprise-intake.ts, scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts and their specs, the enterprise-intake fixture's README and driver, scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts and its spec, examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/shift.ts (`queueOrder` and `ticketStatuses` only), .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (the enterprise notes of 2026-09-28).

## Build

1. The request. The owner adds data/enterprise/requests/<name>.md from GitHub's web editor, so it must be easy to write on a phone: a first line `# <title>` and free text describing what they want, and nothing else required. A README in that directory (a bilingual pair) says how to write one, with one example. Requests are trusted input: only people with push access to the branch can add them.
2. The intake answers requests first. Every intake run, before and independently of the `--min-open` refill, finds each request that no ticket answers yet. A ticket answers a request when its `source.path` is that request's file. For up to `--max-requests <n>` of them (default 2), in file-name order, the run has a coordinator department turn the request into exactly one ticket:
   - the seat whose code or document the request is about, which must exist in the roster;
   - a scope, a task, and acceptance commands that fail before the change, admitted by the same deterministic rules as every other ticket;
   - `source: { path: <the request file>, anchor: <its title line> }`.
   Reuse the intake program and its coordinator presets instead of building a parallel mechanism; a request run and a refill run may be one program. A request admission refuses is recorded with the reason in the intake record, and the next run retries it, so an owner who edits the request gets a new attempt. A usage-limit stop keeps its existing exit code 3.
3. Precedence. A ticket answering a request gets priority 0, and the validator allows priority 0 only when `source.path` is under data/enterprise/requests/. The shift's queueOrder (fewest attempts, then priority, then each division's turn, then id) then takes it before every untried ticket without any change to the engine. Verify that with a unit test of queueOrder in your own spec file. Do not edit the engine's files.
4. Status. `pnpm run enterprise:requests` prints, for every request: its file, its title, and its state. The states are `waiting` (no intake has answered yet), `refused` (the latest intake refused it, with the reason), `queued` (a ticket, no ledger line yet), `halted` (its ticket's latest line neither shipped nor was rejected), `shipped` (with the commit), and `rejected` (the review rejected it). `--json` prints the same as JSON. Derive the states from the files and ledger lines already committed; add no new state file.
5. Tests and docs:
   - Unit tests for request discovery, the answered check, the priority rule in the validator, the status derivation, and the intake's request path, with a scripted LLM as the intake fixture's existing tests do.
   - Keep the intake e2e green, and extend it with one request if its structure allows.
   - Docs in both languages: a "Requests" section in the data/enterprise README pair, the requests README pair, and the intake fixture README pair. Re-record each pair with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
   - A bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (Problem, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Verification).
   - Add the script to package.json and knip.json as the repository does for the other enterprise scripts.

Do not add a real request file; the operator will write the first one after integration.

## Constraints (the enterprise's cycles and another agent run while you work)

- Work only in your worktree. Do not touch /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/enterprise-cycle, /home/user/enterprise-cycles/, /tmp/dsh-enterprise, or the main tree /home/user/deepseek-harness.
- Do not edit these files:
  - owned by the operator: examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/*, scripts/enterprise.ts, scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh;
  - owned by another agent, who is adding cycle records, an evidence report and a deck panel: scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh, scripts/enterprise-publish.ts, apps/command-deck/*;
  - machine-written data: data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl, tickets, shifts, functions and intake records, roster.json.
  If the data/enterprise README pair conflicts with the other agent at integration, the operator merges it: add your section, and do not rewrite other sections.
- Run heavy commands as `flock /tmp/dsh-heavy.lock <cmd>` (typecheck, doc-sync, e2e, broad vitest runs, pnpm build). The machine has 4 cores and 15 GB of RAM, shared with the running cycles.
- Never kill a process you did not start, and never kill by pattern.
- Use no web tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, Firecrawl): they block the whole session waiting for approval. Never disable TLS verification.
- Make no real model calls: every test uses a scripted LLM, and you do not run the real intake. Never pass `--accept-hit`.
- Start with `git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt && git reset --hard origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`.
- Commit with `git -c user.name=Claude -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com commit -F <file>`. Every message ends with exactly these two lines, after a blank line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C
- Never push, never open a pull request, and never touch another branch. Never write which model you are into a committed file. Never commit credentials.
- One subscription serves every agent, and its weekly window is near the limit, so be economical:
  - Read excerpts of large files, not whole files.
  - Wait on a long process with ONE background command.
  - Never poll with repeated turns.
  - Foreground `sleep` is blocked.
- Before your final commit, run these gates: `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run knip`, `pnpm run doc-sync`, your unit tests, and the intake e2e (`pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts <the intake e2e file>`).
- Finish by 2026-09-29T03:00Z.

Report at the end: the commit hashes in order, each command you ran and its result, and what you could not verify.

A self-refilling intake (`pnpm run enterprise:intake`, scripts/enterprise-intake.ts plus scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts and the fixture examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-intake/) has the Program Departments coordinators propose tickets when fewer than `--min-open` are open, and admits them deterministically: the validator, an acceptance that fails before the change, dedupe, contiguous ids. scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh runs intake → shift → functions → roster → deck every two hours with no operator. The enterprise's owner cannot yet give it work except by talking to an operator session. You build the owner's channel: a request committed to the repository becomes a ticket at the next cycle, and its status can be read back.

Read first: CLAUDE.md, docs/testing.md, data/enterprise/README.md, scripts/enterprise-intake.ts, scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts and their specs, the enterprise-intake fixture's README and driver, scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts and its spec, examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/shift.ts (`queueOrder` and `ticketStatuses` only), .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (the enterprise notes of 2026-09-28).

## Build

1. The request. The owner adds data/enterprise/requests/<name>.md from GitHub's web editor, so it must be easy to write on a phone: a first line `# <title>` and free text describing what they want, and nothing else required. A README in that directory (a bilingual pair) says how to write one, with one example. Requests are trusted input: only people with push access to the branch can add them.
2. The intake answers requests first. Every intake run, before and independently of the `--min-open` refill, finds each request that no ticket answers yet. A ticket answers a request when its `source.path` is that request's file. For up to `--max-requests <n>` of them (default 2), in file-name order, the run has a coordinator department turn the request into exactly one ticket:
   - the seat whose code or document the request is about, which must exist in the roster;
   - a scope, a task, and acceptance commands that fail before the change, admitted by the same deterministic rules as every other ticket;
   - `source: { path: <the request file>, anchor: <its title line> }`.
   Reuse the intake program and its coordinator presets instead of building a parallel mechanism; a request run and a refill run may be one program. A request admission refuses is recorded with the reason in the intake record, and the next run retries it, so an owner who edits the request gets a new attempt. A usage-limit stop keeps its existing exit code 3.
3. Precedence. A ticket answering a request gets priority 0, and the validator allows priority 0 only when `source.path` is under data/enterprise/requests/. The shift's queueOrder (fewest attempts, then priority, then each division's turn, then id) then takes it before every untried ticket without any change to the engine. Verify that with a unit test of queueOrder in your own spec file. Do not edit the engine's files.
4. Status. `pnpm run enterprise:requests` prints, for every request: its file, its title, and its state. The states are `waiting` (no intake has answered yet), `refused` (the latest intake refused it, with the reason), `queued` (a ticket, no ledger line yet), `halted` (its ticket's latest line neither shipped nor was rejected), `shipped` (with the commit), and `rejected` (the review rejected it). `--json` prints the same as JSON. Derive the states from the files and ledger lines already committed; add no new state file.
5. Tests and docs:
   - Unit tests for request discovery, the answered check, the priority rule in the validator, the status derivation, and the intake's request path, with a scripted LLM as the intake fixture's existing tests do.
   - Keep the intake e2e green, and extend it with one request if its structure allows.
   - Docs in both languages: a "Requests" section in the data/enterprise README pair, the requests README pair, and the intake fixture README pair. Re-record each pair with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
   - A bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (Problem, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Verification).
   - Add the script to package.json and knip.json as the repository does for the other enterprise scripts.

Do not add a real request file; the operator will write the first one after integration.

## Constraints (the enterprise's cycles and another agent run while you work)

- Work only in your worktree. Do not touch /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/enterprise-cycle, /home/user/enterprise-cycles/, /tmp/dsh-enterprise, or the main tree /home/user/deepseek-harness.

- Run heavy commands as `flock /tmp/dsh-heavy.lock <cmd>` (typecheck, doc-sync, e2e, broad vitest runs, pnpm build). The machine has 4 cores and 15 GB of RAM, shared with the running cycles.
- Never kill a process you did not start, and never kill by pattern.
- Use no web tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, Firecrawl): they block the whole session waiting for approval. Never disable TLS verification.
- Make no real model calls: every test uses a scripted LLM, and you do not run the real intake. Never pass `--accept-hit`.
- Start with `git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt && git reset --hard origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`.

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

s=s.replace(c,d)

en='data/enterprise/README.md'; zh='data/enterprise/README.zh.md'

open(en,'w').write(t)

121:[`scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh`](../../scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh) keeps the cycle's times without an operator session. Started once, detached, in that checkout, it runs the cycle at `ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_MINUTE` (default 13) past every UTC hour divisible by `ENTERPRISE_SCHEDULE_HOURS` (default 2), writes each cycle's output to `<ENTERPRISE_CYCLE_LOGS>/cycle-<UTC stamp>.log` (default `/home/user/enterprise-cycles`), passes its environment to every cycle, and waits for each cycle it starts; at a slot where a cycle started by hand still runs, it waits for that cycle and then starts its own, so a long cycle delays the next one instead of skipping it. A second scheduler exits 4, and a schedule outside whole hours from 1 to 24 or minutes from 0 to 59 exits 2. A container restart ends it, so the scheduled Routine that watches the enterprise starts it again when it is not running.
syntax-ok

content.activeForm: Building the tools, skills, LLM, and prompt-section adapters
content.description: New packages under packages/components/: components-tools (tool kind via tools/change + schemas()), components-skills (skill kind via skills/change + list()), components-llm (model-provider kind via llm/adapters-updated + listProviders()), components-prompt (prompt-section kind via system-prompt/change). Each: src/index.ts, src/invariant.ts, tests at 100%, README triplet, group README row, tsconfig/host refs, allowlist entries.
content.subject: Adapters: tools, skills, LLM providers, prompt sections

content.activeForm: Building the plugin and preset composition adapters
content.description: components-plugins: mirror ctx.loader.entries() as `plugin` components following loader/entry-init and loader/partial-dispose; components-presets: mirror ctx.agentPresets.list() as `composition` components whose members are the preset's rows (plugin components read from the composition file), invoke starts a subagent from the preset when the subagent tool supports it.
content.subject: Adapters: plugins (loader entries) and preset compositions

content.description: Judgment 2026-09-26: kept, re-scoped. The component-inventory phase-3 idea survives only as the goal-4 promotion rule: a harness change (plugin, skill, preset) is promoted when a frozen pair over the hidden-case completion family reads a lift outside the noise floor, and the certificates of that pair are the evidence attached to the promotion. Blocked by the discriminating instrument (#132) and the first powered pair (#134). #3 component_invoke, #4 MCP/Ralph producers, #7 registry docs were deleted the same day: no consumer exists for an invokable inventory, and the composition manifest (slices 1 to 5) took over component identity.
content.subject: Goal 4 promotion path: a change is promoted only on a frozen-pair verdict over the discriminating family (synthesized provenance, certificates as evidence, catalog gate)

content.description: Consolidate the six research agents' findings into a published report (harness improvement, hundreds-of-agents workflow management, papers-to-workflows, OSS repo search, computer use, base model + RLVR stack + compute + EU AI Act), with pricing tables, ranked shortlists, cost models, and what Daliesk reverse-engineers from each. Link from the blueprint.
content.subject: Landscape report: best harness/agents per category with prices (artifact + summary)

content.description: Present a decision matrix (license fit for an EU commercial product, agentic-coding capability, base-checkpoint availability, cost per step, RL ecosystem, sovereignty optics) with a recommended primary and fallback, then ask the user to decide; record the decision in an Agent Note once made.
content.subject: Base-model decision for the 120B RLVR model

content.activeForm: Writing the trajectory export design note
content.description: Bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md: trajectories as a pure fold of the session log (messages, tool calls, results, rewards from certificates and goal completion, provenance: preset, model, components, isolation), JSONL export contract with prior art (verifiers Trace/Task, SWE-smith trajectories, OpenAI chat format), environment registry Service Definition (tasks + completion-standard checks + held-out flag), acceptance criteria, rollout.
content.subject: Design note: trajectory export and environment registry (improvement seam phase 1)

content.description: packages/improvement/trajectories: pure foldTrajectory(events, meta) → Trajectory; TrajectoryService at ctx.trajectories with export({ sessions, sink }) reading ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect; JSONL writer; invariant companion; tests at 100%; README triplet; e2e over the verification-domain fixture proving an exported trajectory carries the certificate as reward.
content.subject: Package: dsh-trajectories (fold + exporter service)

content.description: packages/improvement/environments: EnvironmentDefinition (branded EnvironmentId, kind via merge-extensible map, task prompt, fixture, checks in the completion-standard vocabulary, heldOut, owner, provenance), register() returns disposer, list/get; invariant companion; tests; README triplet; group README + index rows + tsconfig/allowlist registrations.
content.subject: Package: dsh-environments (environment registry Service Definition)

content.description: The adapter advertises `invoke: { tool: 'subagent', arguments: { provider } }`, but the tool-subagent tool takes only description/prompt/run_in_background and is mounted per provider under a configurable toolName. Drop the invoke pointer (the subagent seam cannot see which tool instance is bound to a provider), update JSDoc, README (+zh, re-pair), the 2026-09-01 component-registry note (+zh, re-pair), and both specs; record the gap under Known Limitations.
content.subject: Fix agent-provider invoke pointer in dsh-components-subagents

content.description: Proposed note 2026-09-05-environment-runner (+zh, i18n): a fresh agent per run rooted at the workspace, goal + standard authored from the environment's checks, the runner as validator executing checks through ctx.shell, attempt loop with directives, declared isolation, report, and the trajectory link.
content.subject: Design note: environment runner (improvement seam phase 2)

content.description: packages/improvement/environment-runner: Config {isolation (required), maxAttempts, evidenceMaxChars, checkTimeoutMs?}, run(request) creating an agent via ctx.agents.create with agentDefaultModel selection, goal create+disarm, standard author, followup/whenIdle, check execution via ctx.shell, recordRun/issueDirective/complete, flush, dispose, report; unit tests at 100% with stubbed services; README (+zh); invariant companion.
content.subject: Package: dsh-environment-runner (ctx.environmentRuns)

content.description: examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/environment-run/{cordis.yml,register-environments.ts,driver.ts}: two environments (passing check, failing check), runner with maxAttempts 2, export rewarded trajectories; e2e asserts both reports and the exported reward; register packages in examples/package.json, knip, tsconfig.
content.subject: Loader-booted e2e: environment-run fixture and trajectory reward

content.activeForm: Running the doc gates and pushing
content.description: Update docs/subsystems/improvement.md (+zh) with the runner, SERVICE_PAGE/SERVICE_ROLES/type-link exemptions, model-experience allowlist, regenerate catalogs and graphs (mirror zh graph docs), pairing records, doc-sync, typecheck, lint, knip; commit and push.
content.subject: Docs gates and push for the environment runner

content.description: Write scratchpad/workflow-atlas-draft.md grounded in the repo's seams and processes: principles, roster, W1 harness program, W2 software factory, W3 transcript-to-model, W4 observatory, scoreboard schema, gap analysis of docs/processes, visualization requirements, questions for judges.
content.subject: Draft the four goal workflows (W1–W4) with meta-agent roster, D/S typing, and 100+ metadata schema

content.description: Spawn read-only judge subagents with distinct personas (Factory delivery, Sakana evolution, DeepSeek RL data, Hermes self-improvement, program-analysis determinism, alignment/governance, visualization) over the draft; collect structured verdicts, gaps, improvements; integrate into the revised designs.

content.activeForm: Designing route session continuity for KV-cache reuse
content.description: E2 tier 3 measured the harness loop's spend on the route: 352K output tokens and 554K cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3.0M cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session and re-renders the whole conversation in one prompt, so the growing prefix is written to the cache again each step instead of read. Design candidates: (a) keep one product session per harness session and resume it per step with only the new turn (the tool results as the next user message; native tool_use blocks from the previous assistant message must be paired with tool_result blocks the resumed session accepts); (b) split the rendered conversation into multiple SDK user messages with cache breakpoints; (c) measure first with a probe: same 12-step conversation, fresh-session vs resumed-session, compare cache_read vs cache_creation. Deliverable: probe evidence, then the slice with the route's usage accounting unchanged and a per-step cache-read ratio visible in the scorekeeper facts.

content.description: Spec for the delegated agent (start after #76 merges; both touch packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts). (1) EnvironmentRunRequest.ladder?: readonly { model?: EnvironmentRunModel }[] — attempt i runs on ladder[i-1].model ?? the stamped model; ladder length overrides maxAttempts when present; the runner owns the ModelSelectionRef and sets selection.current before each route attempt (installModelSelection already applies it on the next step), and passes the attempt's model to a delegated child; every EnvironmentRunAttempt records `model`; the stamp gains `ladder` (the list) so the arm identity carries it. (2) Transcript interface: the route implementer keeps its transcript (later attempts continue the session); a subagent implementer drops it (fresh child per attempt) and the follow-up text of a delegated attempt must restate the task prompt before the <validation_failed> directive (today the child receives the directive alone, which is why the product loop recovered 0 of 5 at tier 5). Document that the in-process spawn provider is the route's 'drop' arm and that 'keep' on an out-of-process child needs provider resume (gap). (3) Fleet plan and experiment arm carry `ladder`, digested; scorekeeper rows and observatory columns carry a ladder digest beside model. (4) Keyless e2e in the environment-run fixture (a two-step ladder switching between two cli-mock models, asserting attempts[].model and the restated task in the delegated prompt), snapshot if model-visible text changes, README + docs/subsystems/improvement.md, bilingual Agent Note. Then E5 arms on tier 5 seed 2: start strong (opus×3), cheap-then-strong keep (haiku, opus, opus on route), cheap-then-strong drop (same ladder via spawn), downshift (opus, haiku, haiku).
