The operator needs a live visualization of all the agents' work, one that is at once actionable (what needs attention now, and why), shows the big picture (the whole organization and its throughput), and is epic (a cinematic, memorable experience worthy of a flagship client demo). You build the Daliesk Operations Center.

## What exists (read first)

- apps/command-deck: Next.js 14 with React Three Fiber, four views (Enterprise constellation, Process pipeline, Code-safety city, Workflow graph), deployed as a static export on GitHub Pages at https://lbjlincoln.github.io/deepseek-harness/ (see .github/workflows for the deploy and its path filters). It reads one HTTP feed (`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL`, the `?feed=` parameter) and falls back to committed fixtures under public/fixtures. Read apps/command-deck/README.md, deck/feed.ts, deck/stream.ts, deck/store.ts, and components/enterprise/.
- scripts/harness-feed.ts: the feed server over run directories.
- apps/command-deck/mirror: a relay on a Supabase project (schema.sql, functions ingest/feed/deck, pusher.mjs) that lets the static public deck read a feed from this container, which accepts no inbound connections. Its write token lived in $HOME/.dsh-mirror-token and was erased by the 22:07Z container reset; the relay keeps only the token's SHA-256 in feed_config. You have the Supabase MCP tools (ToolSearch for `mcp__Supabase__`): find the project (list_projects, get_project), restore it if it is paused, check its tables and edge functions, and rotate the token (delete or replace the digest with execute_sql, then bootstrap a new token stored outside the repository). Document the rotation as a runbook step, because every container reset needs it. Never commit a token or print it.
- The enterprise's activity sources on this machine:
  - data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl (ticket and function lines), roster.json (147 seats, 10 divisions);
  - cycles run by scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh → scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh with logs in /home/user/enterprise-cycles/ (step lines `enterprise-cycle: <cycle> <step> exit=<n> at <time>`);
  - shifts in /tmp/dsh-enterprise/<shift>/: run.log, repo/program-*/t-nnnn department worktrees, .sessions/ session event logs; the departments' Claude Code sessions under /root/.claude/projects/-tmp-dsh-enterprise-*;
  - the intake's coordinators; the enterprise functions (gates, CI reads);
  - the nightly Proving Ground bench (`pnpm run bench -- loop`, /tmp/nightly-loop.log, records under data/proving-ground);
  - the operator's own background agents: Claude Code subagent transcripts in /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/subagents/agent-*.jsonl, each with a .meta.json;
  - Branch CI runs (GitHub REST API, unauthenticated through the proxy with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, as scripts/enterprise-functions.ts does).
  - Another agent is adding data/enterprise/cycles/<cycle>.json records, `pnpm run enterprise:report`, and a "last 24 hours" panel in the deck's Enterprise view; build on their work when it lands and do not duplicate it. A third agent is adding owner requests (data/enterprise/requests/). A fourth is building a public /briefing page in the deck. Coordinate by keeping your changes to your own route and components, and rebase often.

## Build

1. An operations collector, a TypeScript script under scripts/ (for example scripts/enterprise-ops.ts). It folds all the sources above into one live operations snapshot:
   - every agent currently working: kind (cycle step, department, reviewer, coordinator, function gate, bench cell, operator agent), seat and division when it has one, what it is doing now (last tool call or step), elapsed time, and tokens where known;
   - the attention queue: red CI with the failing job, halted or rejected tickets, failed cycle steps, a stale scheduler (no cycle in more than 2.5 hours), a stuck agent (no event in more than 20 minutes), disk or memory pressure, and open owner requests. Rank each item by severity, and give it the evidence link (a GitHub commit, CI run or ledger line) and the next action;
   - the big picture: seats occupied and active by division, tickets queued, shipped, rejected and halted, cycles in the last 24 hours, throughput per hour, and the latest shipped commits with their CI verdicts.
   The snapshot is JSON, with a schema documented in the deck's contract (deck/contract.ts). The collector must degrade honestly: an unreadable source is reported as unknown, never guessed.
2. Live transport:
   - Extend the feed contract with an `/ops` path (served by harness-feed.ts and by the relay's feed function; the relay stores it through the ingest function like the other JSON paths), plus an event stream for agent activity if the existing SSE contract fits.
   - A loop (scripts/enterprise-ops-live.sh, detached like scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh: one-function body, flock single instance) runs the collector every OPS_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 15) and pushes to the relay.
   - Also write apps/command-deck/public/fixtures/ops.json when the cycle publishes, so the Pages deck shows a recent snapshot even without the relay.
   - The public deck must work in three modes, and must say which one it is in: live (relay), recent (fixture with its age), offline.
3. The Operations view: a new route, for example /ops, with key 5, linked from the deck's shell. It serves three audiences:
   - an executive glancing for 10 seconds: the big picture and whether anything is on fire;
   - an operator: an actionable attention queue with evidence links and next actions;
   - a client demo: an epic live scene in which the 147 seats light up as agents work, flows run from intake to shift to review to CI to ship, and completions pulse.
   Use the deck's existing visual language (palette, motion, three scenes) and the dataviz standards: legible type, one scale, colour by job, accessible contrast in both themes, a reduced-motion fallback, and a phone-width layout. A timeline or swimlanes of the last 24 hours shows every agent run by kind. Nothing in it may be fake: every number comes from the snapshot, and a replayed fixture is labelled as a replay.
4. Tests for the collector: unit tests with fixtures, covering each source's parser, the severity ranking, and honest unknowns. Keep the deck's tests and `next build` clean, including the static export `DECK_STATIC=1` with the Pages base path. Take a Playwright screenshot of /ops from a local static build at 1440×900 and 390×844, using headless Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, and look at them. Commit them under apps/command-deck/docs/ as the deck's other screenshots are.
5. Docs in both languages: the deck README pair (the new view, the ops contract, live modes) and the mirror README pair (the ops path and the token rotation runbook). Write a bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/. Re-record pairs with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
6. When pushed, start the ops loop detached from a dedicated worktree (`git -C /home/user/deepseek-harness worktree add /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/ops-live -B ops-live origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` there), with any needed secrets read from files outside the repository. Verify the public deck (https://lbjlincoln.github.io/deepseek-harness/ops/ after the Pages deploy) reads the live relay; if the proxy's TLS interception blocks a headless browser, verify with curl against the relay's feed function instead, and say which you did. Report the exact start commands and the token-rotation steps so the operator's watchdog can restart everything after a reset.

## Landing your work (a reset erases every unpushed commit)

Push working slices as soon as their gates pass, in this order: collector first, then transport, then view:

```
git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
git rebase origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
git push origin HEAD:claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
```

- Retry a network failure after 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds; on a rejection, fetch, rebase, and push again.
- Resolve conflicts yourself, keeping other agents' work.
- Never force-push, never push another branch, and never open a pull request.

## Constraints

- Do not touch /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/enterprise-cycle, /tmp/dsh-enterprise (read only), or the operator's tree /home/user/deepseek-harness, except to add worktrees.
- Do not edit the enterprise engine, scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh, scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh, or machine-written data (ledger, tickets, shifts, roster).
- Run heavy commands (typecheck, lint, doc-sync, next build, broad test runs, pnpm build) as `flock /tmp/dsh-heavy.lock <cmd>`. The machine has 4 cores, 15 GB of RAM and 8 GB of swap, shared with the cycles and four other agents.
- Never kill a process you did not start, and never kill by pattern.
- Use no web tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, Firecrawl): they block the session waiting for approval. Never disable TLS verification.
- Start with `git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt && git reset --hard origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`.
- Commit with `git -c user.name=Claude -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com commit -F <file>`. Every message ends with exactly these two lines, after a blank line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C
- Never write which model you are into a committed file. Never commit credentials.
- Wait on a long process with ONE background command. Foreground `sleep` is blocked.
- Target: the collector and the live view landed by 2026-09-29T06:00Z, and polish by 09:00Z.

Report at the end: the pushed commits, the loop start commands, the relay status, what the screenshots show, and what you could not verify.

input.description: Client-grade executive briefing
input.prompt:
You are working in the DeepSeek Harness repository, which houses "Daliesk", an AI enterprise that the operator must present to a Fortune 500 client. The operator judges that nothing they can currently show the client is worthy of a Fortune 500 company. You build the client-facing briefing: the thing the operator opens in front of a CIO, CISO and CFO. It must be impeccable in substance and in form, and strictly true.

## Material (read before writing; cite files and commits, never invent)

- What Daliesk is and how it runs: data/enterprise/README.md (roster of 147 seats in 10 divisions, the ticket queue, shifts, the ledger, functions, the cycle, the scheduler), .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-*.md, and data/enterprise/roster.json and ledger.jsonl. Tickets are implemented by seat departments, reviewed by a blind reviewer that never saw the implementation, certified by acceptance checks, CI-verified on GitHub, and shipped as one commit each.
- The harness itself: README.md, docs/architecture.md; everything is a plugin, on vendored Cordis.
- Measured evidence:
  - data/proving-ground: a benchmark of 44 environments with frozen paired experiments and bootstrap intervals; dashboard.html and the records README; the results note .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.md.
  - data/code-safety: real security reviews of OWASP NodeGoat and a Java Struts app, recall against ground truth, and the three-tier comparison. Also the self-review of 2026-09-28.
  - Branch CI history for LBJLincoln/deepseek-harness, readable via the GitHub REST API unauthenticated through the proxy with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, as scripts/enterprise-functions.ts does.
- Governance and safety mechanisms: the read barrier, sandboxing (bubblewrap/Landlock), the blind judge, sign-off (dsh-signoff), data-use terms, redaction of credentials, and the audit trail (ledger, records, transcripts). Find each in docs and notes.
- The public command deck: apps/command-deck, live at https://lbjlincoln.github.io/deepseek-harness/. Other agents are building an /ops live operations view and a "last 24 hours" panel there. You own a new /briefing route. Keep your changes to your route, its components and data, rebase often, and do not edit their files.

## Build

1. A data builder: a TypeScript script under scripts/ (for example scripts/enterprise-briefing.ts, run by `pnpm run enterprise:briefing`). It computes every number the briefing shows from committed data (plus CI verdicts from the GitHub API) into apps/command-deck/public/fixtures/briefing.json, with each figure's source path and computation. Any figure it cannot compute is omitted or marked unknown, never estimated. The enterprise cycle already runs `pnpm run enterprise:publish`. Add your builder to that publish step only if you can do so without editing scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh; otherwise document the command and the operator will wire it.
2. The /briefing page in the command deck, an executive narrative of about 6 to 9 sections:
   - the one-line proposition, and what is running right now;
   - the operating model: an org chart of divisions, and the flow from intake to shift, review, CI and ship, as a clear diagram;
   - proof: shipped work with CI verdicts, occupancy by division, cycles run, benchmark results with their intervals, and security-review recall against ground truth, each figure with a "source" affordance;
   - governance, security and auditability, in the language a CISO uses;
   - economics, only where the data supports it (for example tokens and seconds per shipped ticket from the ledger);
   - honest limits and risks;
   - the roadmap and the engagement model.
   Fortune 500 standard of form:
   - restrained, confident typography and a considered palette consistent with the deck's identity;
   - generous whitespace, and charts that follow the dataviz rules (one scale, direct labels, accessible colours, light and dark);
   - no hype words and no metaphors: plain, precise business English, with French available if the deck already localizes (it has a French executive summary tradition in data/code-safety; decide from the codebase);
   - a print stylesheet so browser "Print to PDF" yields a clean, paginated A4 and Letter document with page numbers and source footnotes;
   - phone-width layout; it must build in the static export (`DECK_STATIC=1` with the Pages base path).
3. A one-page executive summary: docs/client/daliesk-executive-summary.md and its .zh.md pair. It follows the repository's bilingual documentation rules (docs/AGENTS.md; re-record with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`) and carries the same figures as briefing.json, generated or checked against it.
4. Take Playwright screenshots of /briefing from a local static build at 1440×900 and 390×844, using headless Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, plus a PDF print of it (Chromium `page.pdf`). Commit the PNGs under apps/command-deck/docs/, and look at every page of them. Iterate until you would stake your reputation on showing it to a Fortune 500 CIO: nothing clipped, no overlapping labels, no placeholder text, no number without a source.
5. Tests: unit tests for the builder (each figure's computation on fixture data, and the unknown handling). Keep the deck's tests and `next build` clean. Update the deck README pair, and write a bilingual Agent Note under .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/ (Problem, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Verification). Gates: `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run knip`, `pnpm run doc-sync`, the deck build and tests.

## Landing your work (a reset erases every unpushed commit)

Push working slices as soon as their gates pass, in this order: the builder and data first, then the page, then the summary:

```
git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
git rebase origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
git push origin HEAD:claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt
```

- Retry a network failure after 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds; on a rejection, fetch, rebase, and push again.
- Resolve conflicts yourself, keeping other agents' work.
- Never force-push, never push another branch, and never open a pull request.

## Constraints

- Do not touch /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/*, other than your own, or /tmp/dsh-enterprise, or the operator's tree /home/user/deepseek-harness.
- Do not edit the enterprise engine, scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh, scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh, or machine-written data.
- Run heavy commands (typecheck, lint, doc-sync, next build, broad test runs, pnpm build) as `flock /tmp/dsh-heavy.lock <cmd>`. The machine has 4 cores, 15 GB of RAM and 8 GB of swap, shared with the cycles and other agents.
- Never kill a process you did not start, and never kill by pattern.
- Use no web tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, Firecrawl). Never disable TLS verification.
- Start with `git fetch origin claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt && git reset --hard origin/claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, then `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`.
- Commit with `git -c user.name=Claude -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com commit -F <file>`. Every message ends with exactly these two lines, after a blank line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C
- Never write which model you are into a committed file. Never commit credentials.
- Wait on a long process with ONE background command. Foreground `sleep` is blocked.
- Target: the builder and page landed by 2026-09-29T07:00Z, and polished by 10:00Z.

Report at the end: the pushed commits, the figures the briefing shows with their sources, what the screenshots and PDF look like, and what you could not verify.
